svg.title: Here is why this construction cancels (TF6). Let T = Lquiet. Its Hessian at the identity vanishes when one direction has bounded support and the curl of the other is affine on the enlarged support neighborhood. In fact the Hessian of a two-slot term is the sum of the two products of its linearized curl slots. With the first direction fixed, the other slot evaluated at displacement zγ is A + F(zγ), with F additive. Summing over the family gives A P γ cγ + P a F(ea) P γ cγ(zγ)a = 0 by (TF6b). The same calculation applies to the reversed slot order and each signed translate. The nonwrapping and support hypotheses ensure that these displacements are the actual integer displacements; in
